name: Grand Hyatt Atlanta in Buckhead
positioning: Grand Hyatt hotel at Buckhead's busiest intersection, built around a Japanese Zen garden with a 30-foot waterfall
best_for: Travelers who want a Buckhead base near Lenox Square and Phipps Plaza

facts.text: The hotel sits on the corner of Peachtree and Piedmont, at Buckhead's busiest intersection.
The Japanese Zen garden has winding paths, a bridge and a 30-foot waterfall.
The Zen garden is visible from the restaurant, the lobby bar and the outdoor pool deck.
Suites can include separate sitting areas, private balconies, wet bars, kitchenettes or extra half-baths.
Pure hypo-allergenic rooms have an air purification system and hypoallergenic treatment of all fabrics and surfaces.
The Grand Club lounge has a private entry and a dedicated concierge.
The fitness center has cardio and wellness equipment by Peloton, Technogym and LifeFitness.
Peloton bikes can be delivered to guest rooms.
The hotel welcomes dogs and offers hypoallergenic pet beds and bowls on request.
The MARTA Buckhead Station is two blocks from the hotel.
Cassis is on the lower lobby level next to the Zen garden, with indoor and outdoor seating.

highlights.text: The Japanese Zen garden includes an azumaya, an open tea house.
The Presidential Suite has views of Stone Mountain and downtown Atlanta, a private balcony with furniture and a regulation-size pool table.
Guest rooms and suites offer views of the Buckhead neighborhood, Atlanta's skyline, Stone Mountain or the Japanese Zen garden.
The Fabled is a cocktail bar and restaurant beside the garden and waterfall, featuring Georgia ingredients and garden-fresh herbs.
Buckhead Village District, Lenox Square mall and Phipps Plaza are within minutes of the hotel.

considerations.text: The hotel draws a significant business and convention crowd.
WhataHotel notes the urban city-center setting may not suit travelers seeking a quiet, resort-style escape.
